subject: Post-call: Integration action items — auth, routing, embeddings repro
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@brightwave.io>
Cc: Kyle Murphy <kmurphy@brightwave.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap + action items (auth, routing, embeddings)

Samira / Kyle — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear ownership: 

- Goal: wire BrightWave's ingestion pipeline into Redwood's embeddings + reranker flow, with server-side auth (JWT) and routing to a cost-optimized reranker for long sequences.
- Observed constraint you called out: prod requests sometimes return 5xx around peak batch times; you said it was intermittent and seems correlated with long documents (>30k chars).

Action items (we'll own the first two, you own the last):
1) Ben: share a minimal repro request (curl) that reproduces the 5xx and the exact headers + payload you use. Attached sample: redwood-sample-curl.txt.
2) Marissa (Solutions): analyze routing hints + model variants — we'll check quantized fallback behavior and any header size limits.
3) Samira/Kyle: share a sanitized sample document and the run-of-request IDs (X-RW-Request-Id) if available.

Immediate hypothesis: the 5xx looks like a routing/fallback race when the request exceeds our preferred sequence-length chunk and triggers a reroute to a quantized variant that currently has a shorter request timeout. We'll validate with the logs.

Would recommend we schedule a joint debug session next week to repro together (30–60m). I'm including an initial list of things to bring: sanitized sample doc, request IDs, the exact Authorization header format (JWT vs mTLS), and an example embedding config.

Attachments: redwood-sample-curl.txt (sample request), embed-config.json (example), bw-logs-20270809.txt (optional logs you already exported).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samira Khan <skhan@brightwave.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Murphy <kmurphy@brightwave.io>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 14:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (auth, routing, embeddings)

Ben — thanks for the recap and the clear next steps. Adding a few data points from our side: 

- Auth: we send a signed JWT in Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tokens rotate every 24h via our internal key service; no mTLS at the moment.
- Sample IDs: I attached a short excerpt of the request body and one request id we saw when it failed (X-RW-Request-Id: bw-prod-20270809-7b9e).
- Frequency: about 3–6 errors per hour during peak (11:00–13:00 ET). Errors are 502 or 504. Noticed that the requests with failures typically have top-level metadata that expands the JSON body size (we have a ~40kb metadata blob).

Question: is there a recommended content-length or header-size limit on the Redwood endpoint? If our metadata is causing internal routing to misinterpret the content-length, we can trim it temporarily while we debug.

Happy to join the joint session — Tue/Wed next week is best for us.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Engineering | BrightWave Analytics
skhan@brightwave.io

On Mon, Aug 9, 2027 at 14:12 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samira / Kyle — thanks again for your time today....

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@brightwave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kyle Murphy <kmurphy@brightwave.io>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (auth, routing, embeddings)

Thanks Samira — couple quick clarifications and a reproducible curl to try:

- No hard content-length limit for body we enforce at the API gateway, but we do have model/variant routing thresholds that can change execution paths. Those thresholds are based on tokenized length. Large metadata in JSON can push us into a longer-sequence path and an alternative reranker.
- For JWTs: as long as the token is valid, Auth shouldn't be the source of 5xx here (401/403 would indicate auth); 5xx points to execution path.

Minimal curl you can run against our staging endpoint (sanitized):

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_JWT>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-RW-Routing-Hint: embeddings=fast,reranker=cost-optimized" 
  -d '{"input": "<SANITIZED_DOC>", "metadata": {"source": "ingest", "customer_id": "brightwave-prod"}}'

Notes: add header X-RW-Request-Id to correlate in our logs. If you can reproduce with this curl (or send the exact failing request id), we'll pull the /internal/logs and check which model variant served the request and whether it hit a fallback.

I'll have PrIyom look at the logs once you share the request id(s). Scheduling: I'm available Tue/Wed like you suggested; I'll propose times after I sync with Marissa.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <skhan@brightwave.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Kyle Murphy <kmurphy@brightwave.io>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (auth, routing, embeddings)

Samira — I pulled the preliminary traces for the request id you shared (bw-prod-20270809-7b9e). Quick engineering notes: 

- Repro summary (what we saw): request routed to reranker-v2-quant (a quantized variant) after the tokenizer predicted >8k tokens due to the large metadata blob. That variant currently has a lower per-request compute budget and a shorter hard timeout (30s) vs the float variant (90s). When the queue length spikes, the quantized variant responds with 502/504 upstream.
- Why it happens: routing policy is designed to favor cost-optimized variants on long sequences; however, the quantized variant isn't fully warmed for long KV-cache runs and can trigger an early 5xx when CPU/GPU scheduling stalls under burst. 

Immediate mitigations we can apply before code/infra changes: 
1) Set header X-RW-Routing-Force: reranker-v2-float — forces float variant for this customer for a narrow window.
2) Increase the hard timeout for reranker-v2-quant from 30s to 60s for the next 48h for BrightWave (we can do this per-customer via a routing profile).
3) Suggest short-term: trim non-essential metadata fields on your side (we can give a list of safe fields).

I attached a local snippet of the sample embed config we recommend (embed-config.json) and the raw log tail we pulled (bw-logs-20270809.txt) — both are sanitized.

If you want us to run a targeted canary (option 1 or 2 above), say the word and we can schedule it for a low-traffic window. Prefer doing this with you on the line so we can watch the trace IDs together.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

> On Tue, Aug 10, 2027 at 10:03 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Thanks Samira — couple quick clarifications...

From: Samira Khan <skhan@brightwave.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Murphy <kmurphy@brightwave.io>, PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + action items (auth, routing, embeddings)

Marissa / Ben — thanks for the analysis and the suggested mitigations. Quick update after running Ben's curl and swapping X-RW-Routing-Force to reranker-v2-float in our staging: we could reproduce the 502s consistently before the change and it's stable after switching to the float variant. The staging runs had 0 failures in ~200 requests.

We'd like to proceed with option 2 (increase quant timeout to 60s) for a 48h canary on prod and then evaluate if prefix/KV warming will give us long-term reliability. Can we schedule a joint debug/canary window on Tue 2027-08-17 15:00 ET (19:00 UTC)? PrIyom from your team will be helpful for log correlating.

Also: we'll temporarily remove ~3 non-essential metadata fields from the ingest pipeline as a protective measure. We'll send you the sanitized request IDs from the canary once it's running.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Samira
